title: Test score cutoff and college enrollment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) - specifically sharp RDD since treatment assignment is deterministic based on the cutoff. The key assumption is that potential outcomes are continuous at the cutoff, meaning students just below and just above the 0.5 threshold are comparable except for treatment status. This allows us to identify the causal effect of automatic admission eligibility on college enrollment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s26_data.csv")

# Basic data inspection
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))
print(paste("Total observations:", nrow(data)))
print(paste("Observations near cutoff:", sum(data$near_cutoff)))

# Center the running variable at the cutoff
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - 0.5

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var, c = 0.5)
print("Main RDD Results:")
print(summary(rdd_result))

# Extract and print the key coefficient
treatment_effect <- rdd_result$coef[1]
std_error <- rdd_result$se[1]
p_value <- rdd_result$pv[1]

print(paste("Treatment Effect (RDD coefficient):", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(std_error, 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(p_value, 4)))

# Robustness check 1: Manual local linear regression with bandwidth ±0.3
bandwidth_data <- data[data$near_cutoff == 1, ]
manual_rdd <- lm(y ~ treated + running_var_centered + treated:running_var_centered, 
                 data = bandwidth_data)
print("Robustness Check 1 - Manual RDD with ±0.3 bandwidth:")
print(summary(manual_rdd)$coefficients["treated", ])

# Robustness check 2: Different bandwidth using rdrobust
rdd_robust_bw <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var, c = 0.5, h = 0.2)
print("Robustness Check 2 - RDD with bandwidth ±0.2:")
print(paste("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_robust_bw$coef[1], 4)))

# Visualization
plot_data <- data.frame(
  running_var = data$running_var,
  y = data$y,
  treated = as.factor(data$treated)
)

p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = running_var, y = y, color = treated)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "RDD: College Enrollment vs Test Score",
       x = "Test Score (Running Variable)",
       y = "College Enrollment",
       color = "Above Cutoff") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

# Final result
print("=== FINAL RESULT ===")
print(paste("RDD Treatment Effect:", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("This represents the causal impact of crossing the test score threshold on college enrollment probability"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive treatment effect with magnitude around 0.15-0.25. Students who cross the automatic admission threshold should have higher enrollment rates because: (1) guaranteed admission reduces uncertainty and application costs, (2) it may signal college readiness and boost confidence, and (3) it eliminates potential rejection risk. The effect should be economically significant but not enormous since other factors like financial constraints still matter for college attendance decisions.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — test score cutoff; continuity of running variable required; McCrary density test
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Scoring above cutoff significantly increases college enrollment
